target_customer: Consumers who wanted to carry one device in place of many payment cards, and later wearables makers
problem: People carry many credit, debit, gift and loyalty cards in a bulky wallet.
business_model: Hardware sales of a smart payment card at $100 retail, later a wearables payments developer program
product_category: Smart payment card hardware and wearable payments technology

founders.name: Kanishk Parashar
founders.background_notes: Search coverage says he worked at PayPal and eBay before Coin; YC page lists his later companies RCI Navigator and Powder. The 2012 founding year comes from search coverage.

exit.reason: Fitbit bought Coin's wearable payment assets and key personnel; the Coin 2.0 card product was excluded.

technical_complexity.rationale: A programmable magstripe device with display, button, Bluetooth and security needed custom hardware, firmware and manufacturing; it took until April 2015 to ship, after 42 test designs per search coverage.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware know-how helped, but similar one-card wallets (Plastc, Swyp) appeared within a year and the card relied on magstripe acceptance.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mobile wallets and chip cards eroded the use case; Fitbit bought only the wearable payment assets in May 2016 and not the card.

market_need_then: Wallet bulk is a long standing consumer annoyance; the $50,000 preorder goal was met in 40 minutes in November 2013 after a launch video.

branding.domain_note: Could not get coin.com and used onlycoin.com (per a third party branding blog, unverified).

identity.visual_style: Card-shaped device with a display and a single button

branding.brand_signature: The 2013 launch video that drove 40-minute preorder sell-through
branding.community_and_virality: PYMNTS and others describe the launch video as shareable with heavy media coverage; security criticism after launch led to a public response from the CEO.

brand_strength.rationale: The video drove outsized early press and preorders, but the generic name became a search problem later and delivery delays hurt trust.

pivots.to: Wearables payments developer program, then sale of the assets to Fitbit
pivots.why: Coin 2.0 and developer program per company description; the sale excluded the card line.

outcome_analysis: Coin went viral with a 2013 launch video and about 40 minute preorder goal, raised roughly $17M, then took until April 2015 to ship and faced security criticism and rivals like Plastc and Swyp. Fitbit bought its wearable payment assets in May 2016 without the card line, so the exit looks closer to an asset and talent sale than a product success, though the price is undisclosed.
notes: onlycoin.com is now an unrelated crypto education site, so the original site is treated as dead. Series A: TechCrunch January 2014 said about $15M was being raised from unnamed sources; the 2015 shipping article says $15.5M raised, and aggregators date it to May 2014 with Shervin Pishevar, so amount and investor are partly unverified. Seed from Crunchbase as cited by TechCrunch. Whether the card business wound down is unclear; one outlet says the deal ended Coin's payment products while American Banker says it retained card technology. Founder prior employers for Parashar come from search summaries, not a page opened. Balakrishnan is listed on the YC page.
